A free, open-source IPTV player for Android TV, Fire TV and phones. It\'s a player only — it doesn\'t supply channels; you connect the service you already pay for. Nothing you enter leaves your device except to talk to your own provider.

OpenTV is developed openly, with AI doing a large share of the coding under human direction — that\'s stated plainly, not hidden. Because it\'s open source, no single person going away can take it down: anyone can read every line, build it, and carry it on.

OpenTV is free and always will be — nothing is gated. If it\'s useful and you\'d like to chip in, GitHub Sponsors or a one-off tip keeps the updates coming: new features, fixes and support all come out of spare evenings. Entirely optional, and genuinely appreciated.

Find out why a channel buffers: your connection, your provider, or the stream
Another copy of this channel is available.
Test the copies of your channels and open the one that actually plays best.

Most providers carry the same channel several times — 4K, FHD, HD, SD — and each copy can sit on a different server. Some of those servers are fast and some cannot keep up, which is why one copy buffers while another plays perfectly.

Optimising opens each copy for a few seconds, measures how fast it arrives against how fast it needs to, and remembers the answer. From then on a channel opens on the best quality that really plays, and a copy that buffers is passed over.
It tests one stream at a time and waits whenever you are watching or recording, so it never takes your connection. That makes it slow — which is why overnight is the best time to run it.
